title: SkillsFuture support for mid-career PMETs facing disruption
asked: Whether the Ministry of Education will review the SkillsFuture framework to better support PMETs, given feedback that some upskilling and reskilling programmes may cost more than existing SkillsFuture credits.
response: SkillsFuture Singapore provides course fee subsidies of up to 70% plus an opening $500 SkillsFuture Credit at age 25, usable against out-of-pocket costs for standalone courses, Career Transition Programmes, full qualifications and stackable micro-credentials from the Institutes of Higher Learning. Singaporeans aged 40 and above get the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy, raising the course fee subsidy to up to 90%, a $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up for curated substantive courses, and a training allowance of 50% of average income over the most recent 12 months, capped at $3,000 a month. The Ministry will continue to review and, if necessary, calibrate its support.
